clue.text: Earth-it beats lubricant

parts.note: to top something is to beat or surpass it, so 'it beats' gives tops
oil is the standard lubricant for machinery

explanation.surface: Someone claims plain earth outperforms oil as a lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: The fertile upper layer of soil in a garden is the earth a gardener digs.

clue.text: Part of a pub providing water? Hardly

definitions.text: Part of a pub providing water? Hardly

parts.words: Part of a pub providing water? Hardly
parts.note: the name suggests a room with a water tap, but the taps there pour beer

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that any bar in a pub serves water.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tap' is a beer tap on the barrel, not a water tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar room in a pub where beer is drawn from the cask.

clue.text: On paper, just the type to do it

definitions.text: On paper, just the type to do it

parts.words: On paper, just the type to do it
parts.note: 'type' means the metal letters a press uses to make marks on paper

explanation.surface: On paper someone looks just the right sort of person for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just the type' reads as 'the right sort of person', but type is printers' lettering.
explanation.definitionFit: To press inked type on paper to reproduce text.

clue.text: Finishing letter to the old Greek

definitions.text: Finishing letter to the old Greek

parts.words: Finishing letter to the old Greek
parts.note: not a letter of correspondence but the final character of the ancient alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone completes a letter written to an elderly man from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The last character of the ancient Hellenic alphabet.

clue.text: Views of Fleet Street?

parts.note: the opinions of Fleet Street are its newspapers' editorial articles, not the scenery of the street

explanation.surface: Scenery to be seen along a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street in London was the home of British national newspapers; their editorial opinion columns are leading articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper editorials, the leading articles giving a paper's opinion.

clue.text: Night-light for Lassie?

parts.note: a night-light is a star in the sky, and Lassie, the film collie, is a famous canine film star

explanation.surface: A lamp left on overnight for a pet collie.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie was a collie in a series of films and television shows, so she was literally a canine star; Sirius, the brightest star at night, has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is known by this canine name.

clue.text: Wanted a title for a knight, indeed!

annotationWithheld.why: Wanted a title for a knight, indeed! (7): SIR goes inside DEED, so 'indeed' is both the container indicator 'in' and the fodder DEED, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Wanted a title for a knight, indeed!

clue.text: Large depository of jet fuel for domestic use

definitions.text: Large depository of jet fuel for domestic use

parts.words: Large depository of jet fuel for domestic use
parts.note: 'jet' is a gas jet on a cooker, not an aircraft engine; the storage tank holds town gas for homes

explanation.surface: A huge store of aviation fuel kept for household use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet fuel' suggests aircraft; here a jet is the burner of a gas cooker or fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A large holder storing town gas for supply to homes.

clue.text: A rush by the water!

parts.note: not a reed growing beside a river but a surge made by the sea itself

explanation.surface: A reed growing beside a river or lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' tempts as the waterside plant; it is a sudden onrush of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge surge of sea water sweeping onto the land.

clue.text: Book a place for the game

definitions.meaning: to book is to secure in advance
game means wild animals, and a protected park for them carries this name

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a seat for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' reads as a match but means wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure in advance, and a protected park where wild animals live.

clue.text: The times for gifted school, children

definitions.text: The times for gifted school, children

parts.words: The times for gifted school, children
parts.note: read 'gifted' as given gifts: the occasions when schoolchildren receive awards, not times meant for clever pupils

explanation.surface: A schedule set aside for a school of especially clever children.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a timetable for a school for gifted pupils; the comma splits it into school children who are gifted, that is handed prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual school ceremonies at which pupils are presented with awards for their achievements.

clue.text: Lots of beef or bacon for the teams

definitions.meaning: a whole half-carcass of meat, as in a flitch of bacon or half a beef carcass
opposing teams in a match are the two camps

explanation.surface: A butcher's cuts of meat are being shared out between teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher sells halves of a carcass, and two opposing teams in a game are its two camps.

clue.text: Very wrong, to urge a vile act

indicators.note: something very wrong is badly out of order, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that encouraging a wicked deed is deeply wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very wrong' looks like the definition but rearranges TO URGE A; the definition is 'vile act' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity or shocking deed is a vile act that provokes indignation.

clue.text: Rose, going for long walks

definitions.meaning: a climbing rose of the rambling kind
a person who hikes for pleasure in the countryside

explanation.surface: Someone got up and set off on long walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as a verb, got up, but it is the flower: a climbing variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose variety and a countryside hiker share this name.

clue.text: Got it into one's head there's no need for prompt help!

definitions.text: Got it into one's head there's no need for prompt help!

parts.words: Got it into one's head there's no need for prompt help!
parts.note: an actor who has learnt the lines by heart needs no help from the theatre prompter

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly decided they did not need speedy assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prompt help' reads as fast help but means the prompter in a theatre who feeds forgotten lines; 'got it into one's head' reads as a stubborn notion but means learnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt by heart, as an actor learns lines so as to need no prompter.

clue.text: Dream that upset an acquaintance of Alice

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nightmare that disturbed someone Alice knows.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice's adventures in Wonderland were a dream, which makes 'Dream' look like part of the story; it is anagram fodder with THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea-party host Alice meets in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland.

clue.text: Strange pair, not so likely to kill pests

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd couple who seem unlikely to be dangerous to vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' looks as if it qualifies 'likely', but it is fodder with PAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic bait laid to destroy rodents and other vermin.

clue.text: Just the winds for craft?

definitions.meaning: the steady tropical winds that carried merchant ships are named for commerce
a craft is a skilled occupation or line of work

explanation.surface: A sailor says only the winds matter for a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat, fitting the winds, but it means a skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: The steady tropical easterlies are named after commerce, and a craft is a skilled line of work.

clue.text: Accounts for such a check

parts.note: a company's books of account are subjected to a formal official inspection

explanation.surface: Someone explains why a cheque was written.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of a company's financial books.

clue.text: Told quite positively: "It's to be brass-faced"

explanation.surface: Someone was told firmly that it would have to be shameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Promised with certainty, and self-confident to the point of brazenness.

clue.text: Hounds in paper chases?

parts.note: a paperchase is a hare-and-hounds race, but here newspaper staff hunt down stories

explanation.surface: Dogs taking part in a hare-and-hounds paperchase.
explanation.walkthrough: A paperchase is a cross-country game where 'hounds' follow a trail of paper; here the hounds are journalists chasing stories for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists who chase news stories for a newspaper.

clue.text: Bound to cause delays in the Civil Service?

definitions.text: Bound to cause delays in the Civil Service?

parts.words: Bound to cause delays in the Civil Service?
parts.note: 'Bound' means tied up: official documents were tied with coloured ribbon, giving the name for bureaucratic delay

explanation.surface: Something that will certainly slow down government departments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but it means tied: official papers were once tied with a coloured ribbon, hence the name for bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucratic procedure, named after the ribbon that tied official documents.

clue.text: Pithy old writers put pen to it!

definitions.text: Pithy old writers put pen to it!

parts.words: Pithy old writers put pen to it!
parts.note: 'Pithy' describes the reed's pith, from which the ancient writing material was made, not concise authors

explanation.surface: Concise authors of old took up their pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pithy' reads as describing terse writers; it describes the writing material, made from the pith of a Nile reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient writing material made from the pith of a Nile reed.

clue.text: Used artillery to get the Colenel out, we hear

definitions.text: Used artillery to get the Colenel out, we hear

parts.words: Used artillery to get the Colenel out, we hear
parts.note: firing guns on a position, and also cracking a nut open to get the kernel, which sounds like the army officer's title

explanation.surface: Gunners bombarded a position to drive out an enemy officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colenel' is printed for Colonel, which sounds like kernel: a nut is husked to get the kernel out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombarded with explosive projectiles, and stripped of a husk, as nuts are.

clue.text: Providing main dishes

parts.note: 'the main' is a poetic name for the sea, so dishes from the main are fish and shellfish

explanation.surface: A caterer supplying the main courses of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'principal course' but is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and shellfish, dishes that come from the ocean.

clue.text: Corridor booked by the traveller

definitions.meaning: a hallway or narrow way through a building
a voyage or berth on a ship that a traveller reserves

explanation.surface: A traveller has reserved a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallway in a building, and a voyage a traveller pays for on a ship.

clue.text: Where we can buy cheap drink in the ship

indicators.note: in tells us the drink is placed within the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the prefix of a ship's name
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A ship's bar where passengers buy cheap drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop events with reduced prices, where goods can be bought at a discount.

clue.text: Home made from adobe

indicators.note: made from signals that a new word is built out of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A house built out of sun-dried brick.
explanation.walkthrough: Adobe is sun-dried mud brick, so the surface reads naturally as a building material.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling, the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Council house charges!

parts.note: not rent on a council house but the property taxes a local council charged on houses

explanation.surface: Rent charged for living in a council house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, until 1990, local councils taxed homes by a property levy; a council house is housing rented from the local authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British local property tax that a council levied on each house.

clue.text: Midsummer Madness? No, he has it earlier than that

definitions.text: Midsummer Madness? No, he has it earlier than that

parts.words: Midsummer Madness? No, he has it earlier than that
parts.note: the victim of tricks has his folly on the first day of the fourth month, well before midsummer

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a claim that a person's madness strikes at midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: Midsummer madness is foolishness at the end of June; the person tricked on 1 April has his foolishness in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The person tricked by a prank on the first of the fourth month.

clue.text: Drive mad grandee out

indicators.note: out here means out of order or put out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to drive an angry aristocrat out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GRANDEE; 'mad' looks like an anagram signal too but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbalance someone's mind is to send them insane.

clue.text: Put temporarily out of a job, so get hang-up

definitions.text: Put temporarily out of a job
definitions.meaning: barred from work for a time, as a disciplined employee is

explanation.surface: A worker laid off for a while ends up with a psychological hang-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang-up' reads as a neurosis but is the verb, to hang something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone from work for a period, or to dangle something from a support.
